It's incredible to me to see how God uses His people throughout history to bring glory to His name. He uses the weak things to confound the wise; the base things to bring to nothing the wisdom of earthly wise men. God uses physical weakness, hardship, loss, grief, toil, and pain to increase our spiritual treasures and build His Kingdom here on the earth!

This hymn became precious to my family and me several years ago as we awaited the birth of our fourth genetically challenged baby. We knew she couldn't stay with us very long. She passed away at just three days old. After researching this hymn, I was amazed to find out that the man whose story had inspired this hymn had lost eight out of his nine children.

The story of this man is a notable one. His 61 years on earth were marked by grief and loss, persecution and imprisonment. Yet, his dedication to Christ was outstanding, and his fire for God and zeal for preaching the gospel never waned until his last day.

Samuel Rutherford, son of a prosperous farmer, was born in the year 1600. His life began in the small village of Nisbet, Scotland. As we glimpse into his life, we notice the hand of God at work in Samuel’s early years. At only three years old, he was playing with his friends when he fell into the town well. His sister and friends ran to get help. When they returned, they found a very wet Samuel sitting on the grass beside the well. They asked him how he got out, and his reply was, "A bonny white man came and drew me out of the well." His family believed that God sent an angel to rescue him that day.

From what we know about Samuel Rutherford, he had two brothers and one sister. He was sent to school when he was young, and he became a very diligent scholar. He learned Latin and Greek so well that he eventually became a professor. He married Eupham Hamilton around 1624, soon after he began teaching at Edinburgh University. At this time, Samuel was yet unconverted and cared only for pursuing his academic goals.

In 1626, at the age of 26, Samuel came to a clear and saving faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. He said, "O but Christ hath a saving eye. When He first looked on me I was saved. It cost Him but a look to make hell quit to me." From that moment he was filled with a passion to preach and to speak about his Saviour. This change of life caused such a stir in the university that Rutherford ended up resigning his professorship.

In 1627, Samuel took his wife and two young children to Galloway, Scotland, where he began pastoring the small church of Anwoth. As he commenced his calling there he said, "I have received the commission from the royal and princely Master, my Lord Jesus, to preach Christ to the people." His passion was for the conversion of the people, and it is said that he seemed to be always praying, always preaching, always visiting the sick, always teaching and instructing, always writing or studying. The zeal with which he preached and his concern for the welfare of his congregation had a great effect on them. Not only them, but folks came from the surrounding towns and villages to hear his preaching. A friend once reported, "Many times I thought he would have flown out of the pulpit when he came to speak of Jesus Christ."

Samuel was not estranged from grief and sorrow. In 1631, only four short years after he began his work as a pastor, his wife passed away. His two children also became ill and left this world. In 1636, after nine years of preaching, he was banished to Aberdeen, where he was forbidden to preach the gospel. This was a very difficult time for him as he greatly missed his wife and children as well as his congregation, the Church at Anwoth. This time in his life is indeed one reason he is so well remembered, for he began writing letters back to his church people and friends. Out of the 365 letters he wrote, 220 of them were written during these 22 months of banishment.

The government eventually changed hands, which gave more liberty to the non-conformist Covenanters. Thereupon Rutherford quickly returned to his beloved flock at Anwoth. About a year later, in the fall of 1639, he again reluctantly left Anwoth but this time to fulfill an appointment to become Professor of Divinity at St Mary's College in St. Andrews. This change was difficult for him, as he again greatly missed his congregation. He writes, "My removal from my flock is so heavy to me, that it maketh my life a burden to me, I had never such a longing for death. The Lord help and hold up this sad clay."

After five months in his new position and having been alone for nearly ten years, the 40-year-old Samuel married Jean McMath. Together they had seven children. Sadly, six of them died in infancy and early childhood. Only a daughter named Agnes survived to adulthood.

Rutherford continued to be an influential leader in the non-conformist movement in Scotland for the next 20 years until 1660. With the death of Cromwell, the rule of the commonwealth came to an end, and Charles II was restored to power. Once again, the wrath of the monarchy fell on Samuel. He was summoned to appear before the judge and charged with high treason against the government for preaching the truth. He was put in prison to await execution. However, before the king could put him to death, Samuel became quite sick. He said, "I have a summons already from a superior Judge, and I behoove to answer my first summons and when your day arrives I shall be where few Kings and great folks come."

Late in the afternoon of the last day of his life in answer to the question, "What think ye now of Christ?" answered thusly, "Oh, that all my brethren in the land may know what a Master I have served, and what peace I have this day! I shall sleep in Christ, and when I awake, I shall be satisfied with His likeness. This night shall close the door, and put my anchor within the veil, and I shall go away in a sleep by five of the clock in the morning. Glory! glory to my Creator and my Redeemer forever! I Shall live and adore Him. Oh, for arms to embrace Him! Oh, for a well-tuned harp! Glory! glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land!" These words were heard by his wife, daughter and friends, and he was indeed with his Lord by five in the morning.

Nearly two centuries later, Annie Ross Cousin, a Scottish poet and hymn writer and the wife of a minister, was inspired by the life and writings of Samuel Rutherford. She summarized his life in a biographical hymn,"The Sands of Time are Sinking". This hymn was first published in 1857 in the Christian Treasury. Out of the nineteen original verses, only four are used in our hymn books. (in bold copy)

The sands of time are sinking,
The dawn of heaven breaks,
The summer morn I’ve sighed for,
The fair, sweet morn awakes:
Dark, dark hath been the midnight,
But dayspring is at hand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

2. Oh! well it is forever,
Oh! well forevermore
My nest hung in no forest
Of all this death-doomed shore!
Yea, let the vain world vanish,
As from the ship the stand,
While glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

3. There the Red Rose of Sharon
Unfolds its heart-most bloom.
And fills the air of Heaven
With ravishing perfume;
Oh, to behold its blossom,
While by its fragrance fann’d
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

4. The King there in His beauty,
Without a veil is seen:
It were a well-spent journey
Though seven deaths lay between:
The Lamb with His fair army,
Doth on Mount Zion stand;
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

5. Oh! Christ He is the fountain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above;
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

6. E’en Anwoth was not heaven—
E’en preaching was not Christ;
And in my sea-beat prison
My Lord and I held tryst:
And aye my murkiest storm-cloud
Was by a rainbow spann’d,
Caught from the glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land.

7. But that He built a heaven
Of His surpassing love,
A little New Jerus’lem,
Like to the one above,—
“Lord, take me o’er the water,”
Had been my loud demand,
“Take me to love’s own country,
Unto Immanuel’s land.”

8. But flowers need night’s cool darkness,
The moonlight and the dew;
So Christ, from one who loved it,
His shining oft withdrew;
And then, for cause of absence,
My troubled soul I scann’d—
But glory, shadeless, shineth
In Immanuel’s land.

9. The little birds of Anwoth,
used to count them blest,—
Now, beside happier alters,
go to built my nest:
O’er these there broods no silence,
No graves around them stand,
For glory, deathless, dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

10. Fair Anwoth by the Solway,
To me thou still art dear!
E’en from the verge of Heaven
I drop for thee a tear.
Oh! if one soul from Anwoth
Meet me at God’s right hand,
My Heaven will be two Heavens,
In Immanuel’s land!

11. I’ve wrestled on towards Heaven,
‘Ganst storm, and wind, and tide;—
Now, like a weary traveler,
That leaneth on his guide,
Amid the shades of evening,
While sinks life’s ling’ring sand,
I hail the glory dawning
From Immanuel’s land.

12. Deep waters cross’d life’s pathway,
The hedge of thorns was sharp;
Now these lie all behind me,—
Oh, for a well-tuned harp!
Oh, to join Hallelujah
With yon triumphant band,
Who sing where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land!

13. With mercy and with judgment
My web of time He wove,
And aye the dews of sorrow
Were lustered with His love!
I’ll bless the hand that guided,
I’ll bless the heart that plann’d,
When throned where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

14. Soon shall the cup of glory
Wash down earth’s bitterest woes,
Soon shall the desert brier
Break into Eden’s rose:
The curse shall change to blessing–
The name on earth that’s bann’d,
Be graven on the white stone
In Immanuel’s land.

15. Oh! I am my Beloved’s,
And my Beloved’s mine!
He brings a poor vile sinner
Into His “house of wine:”
I stand upon His merit,
I know no other stand,
Not e’en where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

16. I shall sleep sound in Jesus,
Fill’d with His likeness rise,
To live and to adore Him,
To see Him with these eyes:
‘Tween me and resurrection
But Paradise doth stand;
Then—then for glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land!

17. The bride eyes not her garment,
But her dear Bridegroom’s face;
I will not gaze at glory,
But on my King of Grace—
Not at the crown He giveth,
But on His pierced hand:
The Lamb is all the glory
Of Immanuel’s land.

18. I have borne scorn and hatred,
I have borne wrong and shame,
Earth’s proud ones have reproach’d me,
For Christ’s thrice blessed name:
Where God His seal set fairest
They’ve stamp’d their foulest brand;
But judgment shines like noonday
In Immanuel’s land.

19. They’ve summoned me before them,
But there I may not come,—
My Lord says, “Come up hither,”
My Lord says, “Welcome home!
My King now at His white throne,
My presence doth command,
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

The fine complementary tune for this text was composed in the early 1800s by a French musician, Chretien D`Urhan. It is well fitted to the words of the hymn—its solemn tempo matches the solemnity of the words. The rising melodic line of the last phrase perfectly matches the anticipated joy expressed by the refrain—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

As we conclude this hymn history, let us continue to marvel at the providence of God in the lives of those who have gone before us. May we follow Christ with all our hearts and be vessels ready for the Master's use! One last quote by Samuel Rutherford to take with us. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

The information for this article was sourced from 101 Hymn Stories, A Treasury of Hymns, Crichbaptist.org.

समय के रेते डूब रहे हैं,
स्वर्ग की भोर टूट रही है,
उस गर्मियों की सुबह जिसके लिये मैंने तड़पा,
वह सुन्दर, मधुर सुबह जाग उठी है:
अंधेरी, अंधेरी रही है मध्यरात्रि,
पर दिन की पहली किरण पास है,
और महिमा—महिमा वास करती है
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

2. ओ! यह सदैव अच्छा है,
ओ! यह सदा ही अच्छा रहेगा
मेरा घोंसला किसी जंगल में न लटका रहे
इस मृत्यु-निश्चत तट पर!
हाँ, दुनिया व्यर्थ विलीन हो जाए,
जैसे जहाज से खण्ड हटता है,
जबकि महिमा—महिमा वास करती है
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

3. वहाँ शेरोन का लाल गुलाब
अपने हृदय का सबसे गहरा कली खोलता है।
और स्वर्ग की वायु को भर देता है
मनोहर सुगंध से;
ओ, उसकी कली को देखना कैसा आनंददायक होगा,
जबकि उसकी खुशबू से व्यवहारित होकर
जहाँ महिमा—महिमा वास करती है
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

4. वहाँ राज्यभूषण उस सुन्दरता में है,
बिना किसी परदा के दिखाई देता है:
यह एक सुयोग्य यात्रा होती,
भले ही बीच में सात मौतें भी हों:
मेमना अपनी सुंदर सेना के साथ,
सिय्योन पर्वत पर खड़ा है;
और महिमा—महिमा वास करती है
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

5. ओ! मसीह वही स्रोत्र है,
प्रेम का गहरा मधुर कुआँ!
पृथ्वी पर जिन धाराओं का मैंने स्वाद लिया,
उनसे गहरा मैं ऊपर पिऊँगा;
वहाँ, महासागर की पूर्णता को पाने के लिये,
उसकी दया फैलती है,
और महिमा—महिमा वास करती है
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

"मुझे प्रेम के अपने देश में ले चलो,
इम्मानुएल के देश में।"

8. परन्तु फूलों को रात की ठंडी अँधेरी चाहिए,
चांदनी और ओस की भी;
ऐसे ही मसीह, जिससे किसी ने प्रेम किया,
अक्सर अपनी शोभा छीन लेते थे;
और तब, गैर-मौजूदगी के कारण,
मैं अपनी उलझी आत्मा की जाँच करता—
पर महिमा, बिना छाया के, चमकती है
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

9. आन्कोथ के छोटे पक्षी,
जिन्हें वे धन्य गिनते थे,—
अब, अधिक सुखी वेदियों के पास,
मेरे घोसले बनाने जाते हैं:
इनके ऊपर कोई मौन नहीं छाया करता,
उनके चारों ओर कोई कब्रें नहीं हैं,
क्योंकि अमर महिमा वास करती है
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

10. सुन्दर आन्कोथ सोलवे के पास,
मेरे लिये तू अभी भी प्रिय है!
स्वर्ग के किनारे से भी मैं तेरे लिये
एक आँसू टपका दूँगा।
ओ! यदि आन्कोथ से एक आत्मा
मुझे परमेश्वर के दाहिने हाथ पर मिले,
मेरा स्वर्ग दो स्वर्ग हो जाएगा,
इम्मानुएल के देश में!

11. मैंने स्वर्ग की ओर संघर्ष किया है,
तूफ़ान, हवा और ज्वार के खिलाफ;—
अब, जैसे एक थका हुआ यात्री,
जो अपने मार्गदर्शक पर टिका है,
संध्या के सायों के बीच,
जबकि जीवन की अवशिष्ट रेत डूबती है,
मैं इम्मानुएल के देश से उभरती महिमा का अभिनंदन करता हूँ।

12. गहराईयों ने जीवन के मार्ग को पार किया,
कांटेदार बाड़ तेज थी;
अब ये सब मेरे पीछे हैं,—
ओ! एक अच्छी तरह सुरबद्ध हार्प के लिये!
ओ! यज्ञवाहिनीhallelujah में शामिल होने के लिये
उस विजयी गिरोह के साथ,
जो गाते हैं जहाँ महिमा वास करती है
इम्मानुएल के देश में!

13. कृपा और न्याय के साथ
उसने मेरे समय की जाली बुनी,
और सदैव शोक की ओसें
उसकी प्रेम से चमकीली हुईं!
मैं उस हाथ की स्तुति करूँगा जिसने मार्गदर्शन किया,
मैं उस हृदय की स्तुति करूँगा जिसने योजना बनाई,
जब मैं सिंहासन पर बैठूँगा जहाँ महिमा वास करती है
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

14. शीघ्र ही महिमा का प्याला
पृथ्वी के कड़वे से कड़वे दुखों को धो देगा,
शीघ्र ही रेगिस्तान की काँटी
ईडन के गुलाब में खिल उठेगी:
शाप आशीर्वाद में बदल जाएगा–
उस नाम को जो पृथ्वी पर वर्जित है,
सफेद पत्थर पर उकेरा जाएगा
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

15. ओह! मैं अपने प्रिय का हूँ,
और मेरा प्रिय मेरा है!
वह एक गरीब नीच पापी को ले आता है
अपने “मदिरालय” में:
मैं उसकी सिद्धि पर खड़ा हूँ,
मैं किसी और आधार को नहीं जानता,
यहाँ तक कि जहाँ महिमा वास करती है भी नहीं
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

16. मैं यीशु में दृढ़ निद्रा सोऊँगा,
उसकी समानता से भरा उठूँगा,
जीऊँगा और उसकी आराधना करूँगा,
उसे अपनी आँखों से देखने के लिए:
मेरे और पुनरुत्थान के बीच
केवल स्वर्गोद्यान खड़ा है;
फिर—फिर महिमा के वास के लिये
इम्मानुएल के देश में!

परन्तु अपने प्रिय वर के चेहरे पर;
मैं महिमा पर नहीं निहारूँगा,
पर अपने कृपा-राजा पर—
नहीं उस मुकुट पर जो वह देता है,
परन्तु उसके छिद्रित हाथ पर:
मेमना ही समस्त महिमा है
इम्मानुएल के देश की।

18. मैंने तिरस्कार और घृणा सहा है,
मैंने अन्याय और लज्जा सहा है,
पृथ्वी के गर्वीले लोगों ने मुझे अपमानित किया है,
मसीह के त्रि-धन्य नाम के कारण:
जहाँ परमेश्वर ने अपना मुहर सबसे सुंदर ढंग से लगाई है
वहाँ उन्होंने अपना घिनौना छाप लगाया है;
पर न्याय मध्यान्ह की तरह चमकता है
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

19. उन्होंने मुझे अपने सामने तलब किया है,
पर वहाँ मैं नहीं आ सकता,—
मेरे प्रभु कहते हैं, “यहाँ ऊपर आओ,”
मेरे प्रभु कहते हैं, “स्वागत है घर!”
मेरा राजा अब अपने श्वेत सिंहासन पर है,
मेरी उपस्थिति का आदेश देता है,
जहाँ महिमा—महिमा वास करती है
इम्मानुएल के देश में।

The fine complementary tune for this text was composed in the early 1800s by a French musician, Chretien D`Urhan. It is well fitted to the words of the hymn—its solemn tempo matches the solemnity of the words. The rising melodic line of the last phrase perfectly matches the anticipated joy expressed by the refrain—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

As we conclude this hymn history, let us continue to marvel at the providence of God in the lives of those who have gone before us. May we follow Christ with all our hearts and be vessels ready for the Master's use! One last quote by Samuel Rutherford to take with us. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

Part 1

For Alice, life is exasperating. Each day feels like an endless grind. She loves her family, but in her heart, she questions if what she is working so hard to accomplish makes any difference at all. She didn’t always feel bogged down, and she wondered what changed to make her feel overwhelmed so much of the time.

Sometimes busyness increases so gradually that we barely recognize the change. Busyness, given the chance, will overload us with more obligations than we can realistically get done in one day, or one week, or even one lifetime. Then, without warning, we reach the overload point when we feel as though we cannot possibly handle any more. Relentless overload can cause physical and mental exhaustion to the point where we feel deprived of enthusiasm, energy, and purpose. Some women seem to have a built-in indicator of where the overload line is. Others, like myself, struggle to find that balance. Constantly. There are so many good, interesting, and exciting options right at our fingertips; without much thought, we fill our days.

Concepts that contribute to overload

Playing multiple roles can be stressful. Overloading yourself with responsibilities and commitments can make you forget what is most important. It is easy to equate busyness with self-worth. By default, we start believing that:

  • Homemakers are capable of handling everything.
  • Homemakers, especially godly homemakers, are never frustrated.
  • A homemaker should anticipate all her family’s needs.

If we are honest, we know that these statements are unrealistic. Homemakers cannot do everything. All homemakers experience frustration occasionally. A mother cannot consistently be one step ahead of her family’s needs.

Rethinking the busy life

Household duties and caring for our families fill our days. Sometimes those tasks alone make us extremely busy. But what about the extra-circular activities or the high standard we hold ourselves to? We may need to think differently so we can break free from habits that threaten to control us.

Accept your limits

Maybe you can go to a Tupperware party, attend a Bible study, and repaint the bathroom all in one week. But should you? Good homemakers allow themselves to simplify even if they prefer doing it another way. That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.

Evaluate what causes frustrations

Artificial smiles can hide inner frustrations, but it doesn’t cure them. It works best to admit that there is a problem and then seek a solution. I’ve had to learn this repeatedly. All my family members know that we eat dinner at 5:30. But a late arrival habit is trending, and it bothers me.

When I told my husband about the frustration, he simply said, “Why don’t you explain the issue and quit being so uptight about it?” Good point. Proactively seeking solutions works for many problem areas.

Imperfect women make good homemakers

Quit worrying about perfection and make decisions based on what is best for today. Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.

Everyone differs when it comes to how much we can handle. On the other hand, everyone is the same; we all have limits. In future installments, we will discuss how to deal with common points of overload.

Part 2

Many homemakers find themselves stretched thin among commitments that go with home, family, and other activities. As busy as we are, why do we continue to fill our schedules fuller?

It is easy for me to commit to a new project and then realize, halfway into the task, that I have overstepped my limits. Too often, I overestimate the amount of time I must have to complete a project and underestimate the amount of time a task will take.

Commitment overload happens by default. When we play multiple roles and add more responsibilities, we can easily become slaves to the promises we have made. Overload tends to drain our energy, dull our senses, and deaden our joy.

Recognizing Overload

Sometimes multiple activities take place in rapid sequence. Normally, we can flow with short-term spurts of busyness. But if the flow of activities is never-ending and we keep adding more obligations, we develop a pattern that becomes a way of life.

Too many commitments beyond normal duties make us candidates for depression and burnout. Personally, when I experience insomnia, apathy, or irritability, it is time to examine my schedule. If adjustments aren’t made, someone or something will suffer.

No one can overextend themselves indefinitely. Sometimes we suffer consequences for keeping a pace that is beyond our resources. Symptoms of overload can include lack of sleep, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure, and a susceptible immune system.

Breaking Free of Overload

Identifying overload takes an honest evaluation of yourself. How can you know if this is just a busy season or if busyness is the new normal? Are you declining a request because life is too full, or is it an excuse? Do you have to say “yes” on the spot? With practice, you can learn how to pull back before reaching the overload point.

Let an idea or request gel before committing

This has saved me a great deal of stress. There are so many good things to be involved in, and new inspirations come daily. Sometimes tasks can be incorporated into my/our schedule. Other times I must simply let them go and stay focused on what is most important. Consider waiting a few hours before incorporating new ideas and requests.

Seek advice, especially your husband’s

A renowned doughnut maker was asked to have a stand at an auction. She asked her husband what he thought about it. He said, “As long as you don’t complain and stress about it like you did last year, I don’t care.” Was her husband saying “yes” or “no”? This lady should take the cue that doughnut making was somehow adding stress. Either she should not do it, or together they must seek a workable solution.

Evaluate your schedule regularly

Keep a detailed calendar to have a picture of past, present, and future events. If your family had the flu last week and you plan to take an out-of-state trip next week, should you add more? What is the emotional health of your family? Is your husband stressed at work? Sometimes it is better to have a time slot of nothing so it can be filled with what is important now. You can’t do a good job at anything if you are spread too thin. Too many obligations make it hard to be personally refreshed and congenial. Choosing commitments wisely will help you invest your energy where it is most valuable for today.

第1部分

对爱丽丝来说，生活令人恼火。每一天都像无休止的磨难。她爱她的家庭，但内心里，她质疑自己如此努力工作的意义是否真的有什么不同。她并不总是感到沉重，她想知道是什么改变让她大部分时间都感到不堪重负。

有时忙碌是逐渐增加的，以至于我们几乎察觉不到变化。若给忙碌机会，它会让我们承担超过我们现实能在一天、一周，甚至一生中完成的义务。然后，在毫无预警的情况下，我们达到超负荷点，感觉自己不可能再承受更多。持续的超负荷会导致身心疲惫，以至于我们觉得缺乏热情、精力和目标。有些女性似乎自带一个指标，知道超负荷的界限在哪里。其他人，像我自己一样，努力寻找平衡。不断地寻求平衡。太多美好、有趣且令人兴奋的选择近在咫尺；我们不经多想就把日子填满了。

导致超负荷的观念

扮演多重角色会带来压力。让自己承担过多责任和承诺会让你忘记什么是最重要的。很容易把忙碌等同于自我价值。默认情况下，我们开始相信：

  • 家庭主妇能够处理一切。
  • 家庭主妇，尤其是虔诚的家庭主妇，从不感到沮丧。
  • 家庭主妇应该预见她家庭的所有需要。

如果我们诚实，我们知道这些说法是不现实的。家庭主妇不能做所有事情。所有家庭主妇都会偶尔感到沮丧。母亲不可能始终比家庭的需要早一步。

重新思考忙碌的生活

家务和照顾家人占满了我们的日子。有时这些任务本身就让我们异常忙碌。但我们对课外活动或对自己施加的高标准又如何？我们可能需要换一种思路，以便摆脱那些威胁要控制我们的习惯。

接受你的极限

也许你可以在一周内参加一个保鲜盒聚会、参与一个查经班并粉刷浴室。但你应该吗？优秀的家庭主妇允许自己简化，即便她们更喜欢以另一种方式做。这意味着如果你是个热衷烘烤面包的人，把几条面包扔进购物车也是可以的。

评估引起挫败感的原因

做作的微笑可以掩盖内在的挫败感，但它不能治愈它们。承认有问题然后寻找解决办法效果最佳。我不得不一次又一次地学会这一点。我们全家人都知道我们在5:30吃晚饭。但迟到成风，这让我不爽。

当我把这种挫败感告诉丈夫时，他只是说：“你为什么不把问题说明白，别这么紧张？”说得好。主动寻求解决办法对许多问题区域都有效。

不完美的女人也能成为好家庭主妇

别再为完美操心，根据今天什么最合适来做决定。爱玩且快乐的家庭主妇家具下可能有几只灰尘团，但她们散发出的气场会吸引人们走进她们的心和家。

在我们能承受多少方面，每个人不同。另一方面，人人相同；我们都有极限。将在后续篇章讨论如何应对常见的超负荷点。

第2部分

许多家庭主妇发现自己在与家庭、家务和其他活动相关的承诺之间被拉得很薄。尽管我们很忙，为什么我们还继续把日程排得更满？

我很容易承诺一个新项目，然后在任务进行到一半时意识到自己超出了能力范围。太常见的是，我高估了完成一个项目所需的时间，却低估了一个任务会花费多少时间。

承诺超载是默认发生的。当我们扮演多重角色并增加更多责任时，我们很容易成为所作承诺的奴隶。超负荷往往耗尽我们的能量，迟钝我们的感官，麻木我们的喜乐。

识别超负荷

有时多项活动以快速序列发生。通常，我们可以应对短期的忙碌高峰。但若活动的流动永无止境，我们不断增加更多义务，就会形成一种成为生活方式的模式。

超出正常职责的过多承诺会让我们成为抑郁和倦怠的候选人。就我个人而言，当我出现失眠、冷漠或易怒时，就是该检查我的日程的时候。如果不做调整，某人或某事将会受苦。

没有人能无限期地过度扩展自己。有时我们因保持超出资源的节奏而承受后果。超负荷的症状可能包括睡眠不足、紧张的人际关系、拖延、害怕失败以及易感染的免疫系统。

摆脱超负荷

识别超负荷需要对自己进行诚实的评估。你如何判断这只是一个忙碌的季节，还是忙碌已成为新的常态？你是在因为生活太满而婉拒请求，还是只是在找借口？你必须当场说“是”吗？通过练习，你可以学会在到达超负荷点前收手。

在承诺前让想法或请求沉淀一下

这为我节省了大量压力。有那么多美好的事物可以参与，新灵感每天涌现。有时任务可以被纳入我/我们的日程。其他时候我必须简单地放手，专注于最重要的事。考虑在采纳新想法和请求前等几个小时。

寻求建议，尤其是你丈夫的意见

一位著名的甜甜圈制作人被邀请在一次拍卖会上摆摊。她问她丈夫对此有何看法。他说：“只要你别像去年那样抱怨和有压力，我就不在乎。”这是丈夫在说“行”还是“不行”？这位女士应当从中得到暗示：甜甜圈制作在某种程度上增加了她的压力。要么她不做，要么他们必须一起寻找可行的解决方案。

定期评估你的日程

保留详细的日历以掌握过去、现在和未来的事件。如果你家上周得了流感，而你计划下周去州外旅行，你还应该增加更多安排吗？你家人的情绪健康如何？你丈夫在工作上是否有压力？有时最好留出一个空档，这样它就可以被现在重要的事填满。如果你被分散得太厉害，你就无法在任何事情上做好。过多的义务会让人难以恢复精力并保持和蔼可亲。明智地选择承诺将帮助你把精力投入到今天最有价值的地方。

The winter of 1882 unfolded in the small southern town of Tuscumbia, Alabama. A happy, normal two-year-old girl fell desperately ill with a strange fever. The fever came and went, came and went, and came again. The family doctor feared the child would die of the strain, but the child was strong and one day the fever finally left for good. The following day the mother waved a hand past her daughter's face, but the child did not blink. Subsequent efforts wrought no results and a new day dawned upon the family with a blind daughter.

As the child gained strength enough to resume play, the great dinner bell released its peal to all around, but Helen did not respond. Other noises produced similar results and the Keller family came to the stark realization that life would never be the same again. Most of us may never face the grim circumstances that Helen Keller's family did, but each of us will certainly endure hardships tailored specifically by our God.

The human mind is an amazing and intricate creation. Though many have sought to understand it, its operational ability remains incomprehensible to mankind. It is no small wonder that a portion of the keenest insight into the health of the mind is revealed in God's Word. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Fear is the ominous adversary to a sound mind. It towers over the soul and taunts the saint with its menacing derision. Fear can take a sunny meadow and turn it into a lonely wilderness. It can render a grand wedding celebration as dark as a cave, and turn a banquet fit for a king into a nauseating affair. It is the most powerful and devastating tool in the devil's employment. Despite many bold claims, none are exempt from its wielding. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) It is fear that stands to attack and quench all the prosperity of the soul. If we are to resist it in these days, we he must rise with all diligence in defiant warfare.

We do not need to look very far to behold the disarmament and weakening of man's mind. Medication for the mind ranks among the leading prescriptions consumed in America today. This is no pointed accusation at any individuals who may find themselves in need of medical assistance to control their mind. But it takes no scholar to look at obesity and consider the diet, to see rebellious teens and connect it to the infrastructure of the home, or to see men's hearts (minds) failing them and believe that fear is at the root. While some may totally master their diet, few can claim to be accomplished parents. Fewer yet are those who are not, at times, accosted by fear. Though pride and sense may keep the outward man in check, and remaining perfectly calm, the inward man, at least subconsciously, must deal with the strain. Americans love to claim the motto, "No fear!" but our medication consumption tells a different story. Paul claimed no exemption, for he was “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

What do we fear? Loss, pain, and humility. No one likes to lose something that we have fought to obtain. No one enjoys pain. No one loves to be humiliated. Still, we do not need to read far in the Scriptures to realize that these are often the avenues that God uses to further urge His servants down the path into His likeness. There is no insurance on earth that can secure the vibrancy of youth, the love of a family, or the respect of friends. The things that supply us with earth's greatest vanguard are all vulnerable to the risks of loss. Therefore, we fear. Though we lie in bed until the dawn of the morning, we can in no wise increase our stature nor alleviate the loss that God has laid upon our lives. This anxiety only furthers our grief and adds fuel to our fears.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Herein is the keeping of our hearts and minds: prayer, peace, and thanksgiving.

Like a skillful artisan we must carefully weave these two scriptures together on the loom of life for there seems to be a direct correlation between the fruitful - power, love and sound mind, to the “rootful”- prayer, peace, and thankfulness. There will be no conquering of our fears without these things, and every society that is anemic to these ingredients will certainly be handicapped.

Prayer Begets Power

In our weakened condition we cannot apprehend prayer as we ought. It is then we must rely on those who can or perhaps the Spirit, which maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Communing with the Omnipotent Head of the universe is a tremendously bold task. Many will administer prayer as merely a formal task, seeking to be perfectly reverent in it. This is not communing as with a friend, nor is it bold. It is more apt to fall under the description of fear. The remedial therapy for fear is in pouring out all our anxiety, bitterness, and complaint onto our God. The saints of yesteryear had been known to vehemently pour out their accusations and the bitterness of their soul unto God.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

All these spewed forth bold accusations and complaints against God in fervent prayer and none of them offended Him. On the contrary, God had not given them the spirit of fear but of power, and they serve as our examples. It was faithless Ahab who was told to ask of God a sign in the heavens or earth. In his pious reply he refused to "tempt" God. This lack of boldness and abundance of fear is more tempting to God than the abundance of bitterness in our complaint for “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Peace Begets Love

We are all at rest with the things we love. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) A sparkling young child who is at peace with his father worships the man and strives to imitate him. Through the lad's tender eyes, his father's character is unflawed. His skill is unmatched. Even the brand of vehicle he drives is the best, and he emulates his every action. Even though every father knows the limitations of his son's expectations, we all bask in the seasonal loyalty. It is knowledge and fear that undermines this loyal love. An abusive father will destroy such childhood esteem and fear will be its replacement. It was through base fear that the evil servant buried his talent and did not trade with it. In his eyes his master was austere and to be feared. But God has not given us the spirit of fear but of love.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) The soul who is affected by this love cannot but imitate it. He is at great peace with his Father’s love and the eyes through which he views his Father's character can only enlist replication. However dire the circumstances we may find ourselves in, this spirit of love and peace will carry us through whatever opposition we may meet with on life's pathway. Jacob made nothing of the hard service he was to endure for Rachel; the spirit of love to God will set us above the fear of man, and all the hurt that a man can do us.

Thankfulness Begets a Sound Mind

We do not need to study happy souls long to find buried within the bedrock of each one, a foundation of gratitude. The spirit of a sound mind, or quietness of mind, is a peaceable enjoyment of life. We are oftentimes discouraged in our way when the features of our environment do not measure not up to our own fancy and imagination. A mere sober, solid, thinking mind would obviate and defuse such fruitless notions, yet we are all tempted to entertain formidable ingratitude. It takes no brainpower to expose things we disdain, for Satan is certain to magnify and outline every unsatisfactory detail we encounter. We each may think ourselves into a deep cave, but we must thank ourselves out.

Fear of losing our health, wealth, reputation, and happiness is the biggest hindrance to securing it. To focus on our pain is to invite more. To be constantly analyzing our life to see if we are being fulfilled is a sure avenue to ingratitude. The world is constantly asking, "Are we having fun yet?" The answer is, "No". To these souls, life will never be adequate, and they must wander forth seeking the bigger fulfillment that the last one did not secure. It is the fear that we are not receiving our fair allotment in life that breeds discontentment. It is discontentment that produces more fear, and the downward spiral progresses. Such was the consternation of the soul who asked Christ to speak to his brother to divide the inheritance with him. This may be logical thinking, but it is not conducive to a sound and peaceable mind. This offended soul has no root in himself and will forever be wronged in some fashion and spend his days in search of a savior to come and fix the other party. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

There is no earthly level of attainment or perfect environment that will promote a sound mind. It can only be secured through prayer, peace, and thankfulness. This may take some reprogramming of our minds to reach into the subconscious recesses, but we must soberly gird up the loins of our minds and exercise them if we ever hope to obtain “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

Musim dingin tahun 1882 berlangsung di kota kecil selatan Tuscumbia, Alabama. Seorang gadis dua tahun yang bahagia dan normal jatuh sakit parah dengan demam aneh. Demam itu datang lalu pergi, datang lalu pergi, dan datang lagi. Dokter keluarga khawatir anak itu akan meninggal karena beban itu, tetapi anak itu kuat dan suatu hari demam akhirnya pergi untuk selamanya. Keesokan harinya sang ibu melambaikan tangan di depan wajah putrinya, tetapi anak itu tidak berkedip. Usaha-usaha berikutnya tidak menghasilkan dan fajar baru menyingsing bagi keluarga dengan seorang putri yang buta.

Ketika anak itu mendapat kekuatan yang cukup untuk kembali bermain, lonceng makan siang besar membunyikan dentangnya bagi semua di sekitar, tetapi Helen tidak merespons. Suara-suara lain menghasilkan hal yang sama dan keluarga Keller sampai pada kesadaran yang keras bahwa hidup tidak akan pernah sama lagi. Kebanyakan dari kita mungkin tidak akan menghadapi keadaan suram yang dihadapi keluarga Helen Keller, tetapi masing-masing dari kita pasti akan menanggung kesulitan yang dipersiapkan secara khusus oleh Allah kita.

Pikiran manusia adalah ciptaan yang menakjubkan dan rumit. Meskipun banyak yang mencoba memahaminya, kemampuan operasionalnya tetap tak terjangkau bagi manusia. Bukan perkara kecil bahwa sebagian dari wawasan paling tajam tentang kesehatan pikiran diungkapkan dalam Firman Allah. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Takut adalah musuh mengerikan bagi pikiran yang sehat. Ia menjulang di atas jiwa dan mengejek orang-orang kudus dengan ejekan mengancamnya. Takut dapat mengubah padang rumput yang cerah menjadi padang gurun yang sepi. Ia dapat menjadikan perayaan pernikahan megah menjadi gelap seperti gua, dan mengubah pesta yang layak bagi raja menjadi acara yang menjijikkan. Ia adalah alat paling kuat dan merusak dalam pekerjaan si Iblis. Terlepas dari banyak klaim berani, tak seorang pun kebal dari belenggunya. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) Adalah ketakutan yang siap menyerang dan memadamkan semua kemakmuran jiwa. Jika kita hendak melawannya pada hari-hari ini, kita harus bangkit dengan segala ketekunan dalam peperangan menantang.

Kita tidak perlu melihat jauh untuk menyaksikan pelemahan dan pelumpuhan pikiran manusia. Obat untuk pikiran menempati salah satu resep teratas yang dikonsumsi di Amerika hari ini. Ini bukan tuduhan tajam terhadap individu mana pun yang mungkin menemukan diri mereka memerlukan bantuan medis untuk mengendalikan pikiran mereka. Tetapi tidak perlu seorang sarjana untuk melihat obesitas dan mempertimbangkan pola makan, melihat remaja yang memberontak dan menghubungkannya dengan struktur rumah tangga, atau melihat hati (pikiran) pria yang gagal pada mereka dan percaya bahwa ketakutan adalah akarnya. Meskipun beberapa mungkin benar-benar menguasai pola makan mereka, sedikit yang dapat mengklaim sebagai orang tua yang berhasil. Lebih sedikit lagi yang tidak, pada waktu-waktu tertentu, diserang oleh ketakutan. Walau kesombongan dan akal sehat mungkin menahan manusia lahiriah dan tetap tenang, manusia batiniah, setidaknya secara bawah sadar, harus menghadapi tekanan itu. Orang Amerika suka mengklaim moto, "No fear!" tetapi konsumsi obat-obatan kita menceritakan kisah yang berbeda. Paulus tidak mengklaim pengecualian, sebab ia “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

Apa yang kita takuti? Kehilangan, rasa sakit, dan penghinaan. Tidak ada yang suka kehilangan sesuatu yang telah kita perjuangkan untuk diperoleh. Tidak ada yang menikmati rasa sakit. Tidak ada yang suka dihina. Namun, kita tidak perlu membaca jauh dalam Kitab Suci untuk menyadari bahwa ini seringkali adalah jalan yang Allah pakai untuk lebih mendorong hamba-hamba-Nya ke jalan serupa dengan-Nya. Tidak ada asuransi di dunia yang dapat menjamin kecerahan masa muda, cinta keluarga, atau penghormatan teman. Hal-hal yang memberi kita barisan paling depan duniawi semuanya rentan terhadap risiko kehilangan. Oleh karena itu, kita takut. Meskipun kita berbaring di ranjang hingga fajar pagi, kita sama sekali tidak dapat meningkatkan martabat kita atau meringankan kehilangan yang Allah telah letakkan dalam hidup kita. Kecemasan ini hanya memperburuk kesedihan kita dan menambah bahan bakar bagi ketakutan kita.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Di sinilah penjagaan hati dan pikiran kita: doa, damai, dan pengucapan syukur.

Seperti seorang tukang terampil kita harus dengan hati-hati menenun kedua ayat ini bersama pada alat tenun kehidupan karena tampaknya ada korelasi langsung antara yang berbuah — kuasa, kasih, dan pikiran sehat — dengan yang berakar — doa, damai, dan ucapan syukur. Tidak akan ada penaklukan atas ketakutan kita tanpa hal-hal ini, dan setiap masyarakat yang kekurangan bahan-bahan ini pasti akan mengalami hambatan.

Doa Melahirkan Kuasa

Dalam kondisi kita yang melemah kita tidak dapat menangkap doa sebagaimana mestinya. Maka saat itulah kita harus bergantung pada mereka yang bisa atau mungkin Roh, yang bermendoa untuk kita dengan ratapan yang tak terucapkan. Berkomuni dengan Kepala Yang Mahakuasa dari alam semesta adalah tugas yang sangat berani. Banyak orang akan melakukan doa hanya sebagai tugas formal, berusaha agar sangat khusyuk di dalamnya. Ini bukan berkomuni seperti dengan seorang teman, dan ini bukan berani. Ini lebih cenderung jatuh di bawah deskripsi ketakutan. Terapi pemulihan untuk ketakutan adalah menuangkan seluruh kecemasan, kepahitan, dan keluhan kita kepada Allah kita. Orang-orang kudus masa lampau dikenal dengan kuat menuangkan tuduhan dan kepahitan jiwa mereka kepada Allah dalam doa.

Adalah Ahab yang tidak percaya yang diberitahu untuk meminta tanda dari Allah di langit atau di bumi. Dalam jawaban salehnya ia menolak untuk "mencoba" Allah. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Damai Melahirkan Kasih

Kita semua tenang dengan hal-hal yang kita kasihi. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) Seorang anak muda yang ceria yang damai dengan ayahnya memuja lelaki itu dan berusaha menirunya. Melalui mata lembut anak itu, karakter ayahnya tak bercela. Keterampilannya tiada tanding. Bahkan merek kendaraan yang dikendarainya adalah yang terbaik, dan ia meniru setiap tindakannya. Meskipun setiap ayah mengetahui keterbatasan harapan anaknya, kita semua menikmati kesetiaan musiman itu. Pengetahuan dan ketakutan yang merusak kasih setia ini. Seorang ayah yang kasar akan menghancurkan rasa hormat masa kanak-kanak itu dan ketakutan akan menjadi penggantinya. Melalui ketakutan dasarnya pelayan yang jahat menguburkan talenta yang ia miliki dan tidak memperdagangkannya. Di matanya tuannya tampak keras dan patut ditakuti. Tetapi Allah tidak memberikan kepada kita roh ketakutan melainkan roh kasih.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) Jiwa yang dipengaruhi oleh kasih ini tidak dapat tidak menirunya. Ia dalam damai besar dengan kasih Bapanya dan mata yang melalui mana ia memandang karakter Bapanya hanya dapat menimbulkan tiruan. Betapapun mengerikan keadaan yang mungkin kita temui, roh kasih dan damai ini akan membawa kita melalui segala oposisi yang mungkin kita temui di jalan kehidupan. Yakub tidak menganggap berat pekerjaan keras yang harus ia jalani untuk Rahel; roh kasih kepada Allah akan menempatkan kita di atas ketakutan manusia, dan semua luka yang dapat dilakukan manusia kepada kita.

Rasa Syukur Melahirkan Pikiran yang Sehat

Kita tidak perlu mempelajari jiwa-jiwa yang gembira lama untuk menemukan terkubur dalam dasar tiap-tiapnya, sebuah dasar rasa syukur. Roh pikiran yang sehat, atau ketenangan pikiran, adalah kenikmatan hidup yang penuh kedamaian. Kita sering kali kecewa di jalan kita ketika keadaan lingkungan kita tidak sesuai dengan fantasi dan imajinasi kita sendiri. Pikiran yang sederhana dan berwibawa akan menghindari dan menetralkan gagasan sia-sia semacam itu, namun kita semua tergoda untuk memelihara ketidaksyukuran yang hebat. Tidak perlu kecerdasan untuk mengekspos hal-hal yang kita benci, sebab Setan pasti akan membesar-besarkan dan menggambarkan setiap detail yang tidak memuaskan yang kita temui. Masing-masing dari kita mungkin memikirkan diri kita ke dalam sebuah gua yang dalam, tetapi kita harus mengucap syukur untuk membawa diri kita keluar.

Takut kehilangan kesehatan, kekayaan, reputasi, dan kebahagiaan adalah penghalang terbesar untuk menjaganya. Fokus pada rasa sakit kita adalah mengundang lebih banyak rasa sakit. Terus-menerus menganalisis hidup kita untuk melihat apakah kita terpenuhi adalah jalan pasti menuju ketidaksyukuran. Dunia terus bertanya, "Are we having fun yet?" Jawabannya adalah, "No". Bagi jiwa-jiwa ini, hidup tidak akan pernah memadai, dan mereka harus mengembara mencari pemenuhan yang lebih besar yang tidak didapat oleh yang terakhir. Adalah ketakutan bahwa kita tidak menerima bagian adil kita dalam hidup yang menumbuhkan ketidakpuasan. Ketidakpuasan itulah yang menghasilkan lebih banyak ketakutan, dan spiral ke bawah berlanjut. Demikianlah kegundahan jiwa yang meminta Kristus untuk berbicara kepada saudaranya agar membagi warisan dengannya. Ini mungkin pemikiran yang logis, tetapi tidak kondusif bagi pikiran yang sehat dan tenteram. Jiwa yang tersinggung ini tidak mempunyai akar dalam dirinya sendiri dan akan selamanya dirugikan dalam beberapa hal dan menghabiskan hari-harinya mencari penyelamat yang datang untuk memperbaiki pihak lain. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

Tidak ada tingkat pencapaian duniawi atau lingkungan sempurna yang akan mempromosikan pikiran yang sehat. Itu hanya dapat diamankan melalui doa, damai, dan ucapan syukur. Ini mungkin memerlukan beberapa pemrograman ulang pikiran kita untuk meraih ke dalam sudut-sudut bawah sadar, tetapi kita harus dengan sadar mengikat pinggang pikiran kita dan melatihnya jika kita pernah berharap memperoleh “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

道德关系到行为的是非。清洁是免于道德过失或内疚，带有贞洁之意，即个人的廉正。清洁不包含任何本不应存在之物。正如题目所示，本文将讨论行善与免于道德过失和内疚，活出廉正的生命，并保持我们内在与外在不被任何不当之物玷污。

注意圣经如何谈论清洁。“Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

要在道德上清洁，不靠坚强的决心与纪律是办不到的。历来如此，然而在今日科技兴起、邪恶触手可及的情况下，更是如此。

性方面的罪在教会并不罕见。事实上，各族各类的人都不陌生。我们不能放松警惕，想当然地以为我们的孩子会免于社会和人性之恶。若指望他们在败坏的社会中保持清洁，就必须以身作则并教导我们的儿女与青年。我们不能以为一个人外表怎么穿着内心就一定无虞。外表并不能完整叙说内里的故事。法利赛人使外表看起来光鲜，内里却充满败坏。耶稣说：“Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). 我们也应当首先关注心的问题。当心是洁净的，外表也能够被洁净。

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” 内在的黑暗必然摧毁团契并毁坏关系——每一次都是如此。

这篇信息意在带来希望，而不是灰心。如果你有隐藏的暗点，就认罪并除去它。你可以得自由！摆脱撒但掌控、活出一个内心喜乐、坦然透明的生活是可能的。你不需终生掩饰邪恶的黑暗。耶稣愿意赦免并医治。

撒但很残酷。 John 10:10 中，耶稣说，“the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” 一切敬虔的关系。他的兴趣是拆散你的家庭、毁坏你的尊荣并把你送往地狱。与此同时，他以肉体的情欲引诱你，拔剑要捆绑并杀害你。

道德之罪令人羞愧且难以承认。人的本性是当犯错时要掩饰。早年学会掩饰过错的孩子，往往自然成长为对父母、老师和传道人隐瞒事情的青年。这样的人需要学会开放与透明，否则迟早会对伴侣隐瞒。隐瞒导致双重生活，并引向更多的捆绑与破碎的关系。在人生某些角落有封闭之门的人，常会对手机占有欲强，不愿与信任的伴侣分享密码。我们似乎很容易忘记向上帝掩藏是多么徒劳。Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” 我们怎能如此天真愚蠢以为能向神隐藏任何事？更进一步想：我们为何要向祂隐藏？Numbers 32:23 仍然真实地说，“Be sure your sin will find you out.” 神爱你，祂不会让你继续隐藏那些需要被揭露并赦免的事。

性罪同样极具欺骗性。通常如雅各在第一章所描述般发生。我们被诱惑、被引走、像磁铁般被拉离正轨，感到欲望的涌动，确保无人窥见并掩盖踪迹，向禁果又近一步，欲望更强，理性与清晰思维迅速丧失，像喝醉的人一般无法衡量后果，然后发生雅各书1:15所说：“Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” 第16节说，“Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

雅各要我们不要贪恋不属于我们的东西，哪怕是一丝一毫。圣经叫我们奔逃三样事物，其中之一是淫乱，这可扩及到一切性罪。不要涉足；不要多看一眼；远离它！以建造人的事、神和祂方式的思想取而代之。唱首旧圣歌；感谢神我们不能同时想两件事。无论如何，赶快逃离那淫欲的渴望。它会把你带到比你想去的更远的地方，代价比你想支付的更大。把事情的结局想清楚并问自己：若我顺从这诱惑，我会得到我想要的吗？撒但总是承诺享乐，最终却带来痛苦。记住，撒但从未创造任何享乐；他只是取用神所造原本纯洁美好的事物，曲解并以其堕落的形态重新奉上。记住，撒但此刻拔剑是要杀人。逃避邪欲！

不要随从你的欲望。色情极易成瘾，已缠绕许多人。Promise Keepers 的调查说有65% 的男性成瘾。色情成瘾如同酒精或毒品。他们告诉我们，无论是对酒精、毒品或色情的成瘾，大脑都在呼求内啡肽被释放。我再次强调，得胜的男女将是那些像古时但以理一样，在心里立定主意不使自己污秽的人。

这个课题也针对我们的姐妹，以下几个问题颇为适切。你内心生活中有哪些整齐地藏匿起来的东西？人生的失望是否造成一种空虚，使得服用“情绪类止痛药”能暂时让你感觉好些？你的情感连结是否在神所安排之处得到稳固？

要教导年轻女孩对男人保持健康的矜持。不是以傲慢的态度或永不微笑，而是与年轻男性相处时不要过于随便。我们的社会正好相反，从幼儿园起，男孩和女孩就被嘲弄有关特殊友谊。结果，孩子长大后几乎没有保留。性别间在通信上的私下社交应当避免，除非在家庭关系内。这样可以培养青年的习惯，若他们期望与配偶活出坦然透明的生活，将来就不必再打破旧习。这样想：你愿意你的配偶在社交媒体上与异性频繁社交吗？

姐妹们，要留心你读的书。言情小说会麻木对神话语的渴望，并对婚姻生活产生不切实际的期待。这类书让人以为某个对的人会成为你满足与幸福的钥匙。只有耶稣能填补罪给每个人带来的空洞。没有任何男女能给出我们心灵深切渴望的安全与安宁。这心中的伤口不会被创可贴或止痛药所平息。它们只暂时有用，失效之后，心的呼喊更为响亮。不健康的读物会麻木对神之事的味觉，反而制造对垃圾食品与止痛药的渴求。

另一个对姐妹们的顾虑是你在线上花费的时间。追求精致、独特、魅力与美貌的欲望无穷无尽。不要让这些成为你生命的驱动力，因为它们永不会说“够了”，也无法满足灵魂或指引你的儿女走正路。考虑你为举办聚会所花的时间。多年间，我见过一时风行的商业机会和必备产品的名字来来去去。但几年后我们连这些名字都记不起来，与此同时孩子们在成长，如今已成了成年人。思量你生活中的真实需要和你的职责，然后决定哪些会带来永恒的投资。带着孩子的妇女需要限制她们喜欢的业余爱好，因为此时此刻，她们蒙福有不朽之灵的孩子，与孩子相处的时光是一项永恒的投资。记住，你的丈夫和孩子比你去参加另一个聚会更值得你花时间。

我们如何活出道德洁净的生命？

当卑微。雅各书5章说，“Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” 承认我们的需要需要谦卑与柔碎，但柔碎是得胜的关键。彼得前书5:5告诉我们，神赐恩给谦卑的人。恩典最全面的定义之一是神无酬的帮助，赐给人以重生与成圣。重生是“救赎的恩典”，成圣是“改变的恩典”。事实是神将“改变的恩典”赐给谦卑的人。这恩典从内而外改变我们，使我们成为圣洁。这样的恩典必须像我们得救时所寻求的救赎恩典一样被渴求与寻求。这大概是克服任何成瘾的最重要一步。谦卑到每天向神祈求祂的改变之恩。当耶稣在马太23:26教导说，"First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

诚实。审视你的思想、行为、诱惑、挣扎之处、愤怒、欲望、骄傲、苦毒等。你外表所呈现的属灵，是否真如你所表明？剥去表面的光泽并承认需要帮助。

透明。罗马书2:16谈到那日神要审判人的隐秘。我们多么愚蠢以为能隐藏邪恶。我们或许能隐藏一时，但有一天我们的行为要在无所不知的神面前赤裸陈明。现在为何还要试图隐藏？那些隐藏的事可被送到前面受审，如今就能过无愧的生活。要透明；这必须是一个努力的目标。

对自己讲真话。当你受诱惑时，思考你淫欲之欲望的结局。你会得到你想要的吗？这种渴求会被满足，还是只会越渴越深？如果你看见你的弟兄做你正要追求的事，会是什么样子？若你顺从邪欲，三十年后会如何？会带来喜乐还是悲伤？会帮助人，还是使他人害怕？在你被迷醉并丧失理性判断之前，先对自己讲真话。

训练你的眼睛学会移开。你无法控制第一次看见什么，但你能控制第二次会看向何处。养成习惯，每当看到引发不洁念头的景象时，立刻把目光转向别处，直至成为习惯。

教导我们的孩子。从幼年起这应当成为我们心中的重担。若我们不教孩子神照祂形象造我们，需要被保持洁净，别人就会教他们隐秘并使他们感到不洁。亲近你的孩子，并随他们成长教导他们。

节制情感。在我们败坏的社会中，这是一个安全措施。你越远离这点，越容易被败坏所侵蚀。把你的配偶放在生命的首位，与之分享并在情感上相连。

远避情欲与淫乱。逃离它们！这些渴望是必须被打破的成瘾。记住，喂养什么它就生长，饿死什么它就消亡。成瘾可以被打破，但你需要喂养神所赐的关系并饿死那些有害的关系。

神造我们的方式是：当我们爱神所爱的事物时，心仍然有空间去爱更多。无论我们有多少孩子、孙儿或虔诚的朋友，心仍然能继续去爱更多。但一旦我们开始爱神所禁止的事物，它就会开始替代并毁坏其他一切的爱，填满我们的心以空虚、痛苦与孤独，最终落得苦涩的结局。

许多男人回过神来，看见自己所走之路的极端愚蠢。有些人试图隐藏不洁行为并成功到晚年。另一些人则维持隐藏直到身后。值得深思的问题是：这值得吗？答案当然是响亮的“不”！

何等美好，能活出无愧的公开生活，与神和好，确信罪已得赦免，终有一天我们将被从这邪恶的世界带走，迎入我们圣洁神的面前。

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender
